title: The Frog Pond dance hall and the name 'Jazz'
summary: Moore sat in on drums at the Frog Pond; Welburn notes that a man named Jazz in about 1916 is an early use of the word.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: About how old were you when you were...? You were about fourteen or fifteen?
Oh, I must have been around...
Or you were a little older.

Fourteen or fifteen years old. Now, I left home when I was fourteen. Before... Well, I got started at home... I used to... A place called the Frog Pond. I used to go down to the Frog Pond; they had a dance hall upstairs -- just piano-drums. I had to give the boy 25 cents during intermission. They let me set up all the drums, and I played a little bit on the drums. I didn't know what I was doing. I just rode the rhythm, you know.

I was interested in the name that this fellow had, "Jazz," and if it was around, say, 1915 do you think, or 1916, before the United States got involved in the First World War...? Do you think it was that early?

I see. It's interesting that he would have the name Jazz, when not very many instances, apparently, of the use of the name of Jazz or the word "Jazz" were apparent at that time, or at least according to what we have known so far. That's an interesting little bit of historical information.
